title: Golden decks and the signed SHA256SUMS get CRLF on a Windows checkout (core.autocrlf), failing the LS-DYNA and Nastran golden tests
body:
### Observed failure

On a Windows checkout with Git's default `core.autocrlf=true`, `cargo xtask ci` fails in `decks test lsdyna` and `decks test nastran`:

```
thread 'golden_cantilever_modes_in_cases' panicked at crates\decks\tests\lsdyna.rs:207:5:
cantilever_modes.k differs from the golden file (FIELDCRAFT_BLESS=1 rewrites it)
```

and the same for `cantilever.k`, `solids.k`, `plate.k`, with the Nastran goldens alike. The writers emit LF; the checked-out golden files are CRLF (`git ls-files --eol` reports `i/lf w/crlf`), so the byte comparison fails although the text is identical. `crates/update/tests/data/SHA256SUMS.txt` and its `.minisig` are converted the same way, which the signature check cannot survive once a test reads them from the tree.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows with `git config --global core.autocrlf true` (the Git for Windows default): `git clone`, `cargo test -p fieldcraft-decks`.
2. `git ls-files --eol crates/decks/tests/lsdyna/*.k` shows `i/lf w/crlf`.

### Evidence

The full `cargo xtask ci` output from our Windows run of develop (one `FAIL` per deck format, all four LS-DYNA golden tests, every other test of the crate passing). Normalising the fixtures back to LF makes the tests pass without any change to their text.

### Expected behaviour

The golden tests compare what the writer produces with the committed bytes, independent of the checkout's line-ending setting; CI's nightly Windows job presumably passes because the runner's Git is configured with `autocrlf=false` (actions/checkout) — a contributor's clone is not.

### Investigation

The repository has no `.gitattributes`, so Git applies the user's `autocrlf`. Pinning the byte-exact fixtures fixes it:

```
# Golden decks and signed manifests must keep their committed bytes on Windows.
crates/decks/tests/abaqus/*.inp text eol=lf
crates/decks/tests/lsdyna/*.k text eol=lf
crates/decks/tests/golden/nastran/*.bdf text eol=lf
crates/update/tests/data/SHA256SUMS.txt text eol=lf
crates/update/tests/data/SHA256SUMS.txt.minisig text eol=lf
```

(`* text=auto eol=lf` for the whole tree would be the stricter form; the file list above is the minimum that makes the tests pass.) Alternatively the golden comparison could normalise `\r\n` to `\n` before comparing, but the signed manifest needs its exact bytes either way. Happy to open the PR.

### Version and platform

develop at 417c0c8, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 x86_64, Git for Windows with `core.autocrlf=true`, rustc 1.99.1.
